  The two companies Ill be discussing in this article are longtime dividend payers in the consumer and healthcare industries. Both  Procter & Gamble ( PG +0.67% ) and  Johnson & Johnson ( JNJ -1.02% ) have earned the title of Dividend King . These companies have survived many downturns and will most likely survive more. However, only one of them has an edge over the other with long-term growth prospects. 

  The case for Procter & Gamble  

 Procter & Gamble is known globally for brands such as Pampers, Tide, and Gillette. P&G has consistently increased its dividend over the last 66 years, illustrating its stability in the face of market volatility. 

  The credit could be given to P&Gs diverse business model that has allowed it to stay stable for years and return wealth to shareholders. The company generated $14 billion in free cash flow (or 95% of its net earnings) for the fiscal year, allowing it to pay out $9 billion in dividends. In addition, the company ended fiscal 2023 with a sizable cash balance of $8.2 billion. 

  Yet the company expects free cash flow to be around 90% of net earnings for the entire year. This will allow it to pay out $9 billion in dividends and repurchase $5 billion to $6 billion in common stock. In addition, the company anticipates a 3% to 4% increase in revenue over the previous fiscal year. Diluted EPS could increase by 6% to 9% over last year.

ceramic.snippet:
Academy Sports & Outdoors reported a 6.7% increase in net sales to $1.44 billion for the thirteen weeks ended May 2, 2026. Net income grew to $52.7 million, or $0.80 per diluted share, up from $46.1 million, or $0.68 per diluted share, in the same period last year. The company also announced a debt refinancing completed on May 14, 2026, including the issuance of $500 million in new senior secured notes and an amendment to its ABL facility, extending its maturity to 2031. Additionally, a quarterly dividend of $0.15 per share was declared.

  Academy Sports + Outdoors announced its first quarter fiscal 2026 financial results, reporting a 6.7% increase in total sales to $1.442 billion and a 2.9% growth in comparable sales. Diluted GAAP EPS rose 17.6% to $0.80, while Adjusted Diluted EPS increased 22.4% to $0.93. The company opened two new stores and raised its full-year guidance, citing strong Q1 performance. eCommerce sales saw a significant increase of 17.4%.

  Academy Sports & Outdoors, Inc. held its 2026 Annual Meeting of Stockholders, where shareholders elected three Class III directors, ratified Deloitte & Touche LLP as the independent auditor, and approved executive compensation on an advisory basis. Additionally, the Board of Directors appointed Shannon Hennessy to the Compensation Committee and Clay Johnson to the Audit Committee, effective immediately.

  Academy Sports & Outdoors, Inc.s wholly-owned subsidiary, Academy, Ltd., issued $500 million aggregate principal amount of 5.875% Senior Secured Notes due 2031 in a private placement. The net proceeds from these notes were primarily used to fund the redemption of all outstanding senior secured notes due 2027 and to voluntarily prepay all outstanding amounts owed under its $400 million senior secured term loan. ## Did JNJ Beat Earnings? Q2 2025 Results
Yes.
Johnson & Johnson reported Q2 2025 earnings of $2.77 a share on Jul 16, 2025, beating the $2.68 consensus estimate by 3.4%.
Revenue was $23.7B against a $22.9B estimate.
Johnson & Johnson capped a strong second quarter with results that cleared Wall Street's bar on both the top and bottom lines, as the healthcare giant's diversified portfolio proved resilient even in the face of meaningful headwinds.
Adjusted diluted EPS came in at $2.77, beating the $2.68 consensus by 3.43%, while revenue climbed 5.8% year over year to $23.74 billion, topping expectations of $22.86 billion by 3.88%.
...

Johnson & Johnson raised its full-year 2025 guidance, increasing reported sales growth at the midpoint by $2 billion to approximately 5.4% (excluding COVID-19 Vaccine), and increasing full-year adjusted EPS guidance by $0.25 to $10.85.
Adjusted operational EPS was increased to $10.68 at the midpoint.
